fieldMarks: Larger than other hares: 3-5 kg and 48-60 cm long, with large, heavily padded feet and strong claws.
Winter coat long, thick and white with black-tipped ears.
Summer coat brownish-gray or gray-blue; chest and belly fur stays gray year-round.
Young are gray, with more black in their summer fur than adults.
behavior: When alarmed stands and hops on its hind legs, leaving tracks that look made by a three-legged animal; runs up to 64 km/h.
Mostly solitary but can gather in groups of 100 or more, with one animal staying alert while others rest.
Willow makes up about 95% of the diet, plus saxifrage, crowberry, dryas, grasses, lichens and mosses; digs through snow to feed.
habitat: Mountainous tundra, rocky plateaus and treeless coasts, from sea level to about 900 m.
range: Northernmost Canada and the Arctic islands (including Ellesmere Island), south to Newfoundland and Labrador; also Greenland.

lookalikes.name: Snowshoe hare
lookalikes.howToTell: Snowshoe hare is smaller and lives in boreal forest rather than on open tundra.
